purpose: Scope boundary record for the retained association 2158 and for the zero-new-candidate disposition; literal source facts only, no correctness verdict.

necessary_conditions.literal: f: P^1 -> P^1 with d >= 2 (Main Theorem, line 131; definitions 85, 95, 101 all impose d >= 2)
K is a number field (arbitrary, not necessarily imaginary quadratic, not necessarily Q); line 131
'whose multipliers all lie in K' - every multiplier at every cycle for every period, line 131; contrast with the discrete-subring hypothesis O_K in the cited Ji-Xie Theorem 5, lines 138
f is a power map, a Chebyshev map or a Lattès map (line 131); 'Lattès map' here is the full class of Definition 3, not restricted to flexible Lattès maps

necessary_conditions.item: maps are defined on the Riemann sphere

quantifiers_regularity_objects.literal: universally quantified over K and f simultaneously: for every number field K and every degree >= 2 rational map f with all multipliers in K. No existence of K is asserted and no uniformity in d or in [K:Q] is claimed.

f rational (i.e. holomorphic on P^1 as a map of degree d); characteristic exponent defined as chi_f(z_0) = (1/p) log|lambda| at a period-p point, lines 175-178; Lyapunov exponent L_f = integral of log||f'|| against mu_f, lines 180-188, so a finite real quantity requiring only d >= 2

quantifiers_regularity_objects.item: repeller condition in the support lemma
quantifiers_regularity_objects.literal: Lemma 9 needs z_0 repelling periodic and z_0 outside the postcritical set P_f (line 211); the main proof uses it only for such z_0 (line 272)

the main proof concludes 'chi_f(z_0) <= L_f for all but finitely many periodic points z_0' (line 304) and then invokes Theorem 7; the passage from 'repelling outside P_f' to 'all but finitely many' is asserted, with the finite set coming from critical/postcritical cycles (line 304)
sigma in Gal(Qbar/K) extended by sigma(infty) = infty (line 154); the sets S_n of lines 278-283 are Gal(Qbar/K)-invariant unions of period-p_n cycles

Z_f (classes with the same multipliers with the same multiplicities at cycles of each period n) is Zariski closed over K by S1998 Th. 4.5 and is finite plus possibly a curve of flexible Lattès classes by MM1987 Cor. 2.3 (line 270); the case f flexible Lattès is settled immediately, otherwise f is conjugated and K replaced by a finite extension so f is defined over K (line 270)

limits_and_normalizations.literal: mu_n = (1/|S_n|) sum_{z in S_n} delta_z, a Borel probability measure (lines 293-294); equidistribution gives weak convergence to mu_f, the measure of maximal entropy (Theorem 6, lines 166-173)

for every m in R, chi_f(w_n) <= integral of max(log||f'||, m) dmu_n (lines 296-299); then limit n -> infinity using continuity of the truncated function (line 300-303), then m -> -infinity via monotone convergence (line 304)
||f'(z)|| = |f'(z)|(1+|z|^2)/(1+|f(z)|^2) for the metric 2|dz|/(1+|z|^2), lines 180-183; this normalization is what makes chi_f and L_f comparable
p_n are pairwise distinct (line 280), which yields S_m ∩ S_n = empty for m != n (line 284) - the disjointness hypothesis of Theorem 6
rho_sigma^(n) = sigma(lambda_n) = lambda_n because lambda_n in K (line 284); then the average of log||f'|| over S_n equals chi_f(w_n) (lines 289-291)

core_recount_boundaries.literal: Lemma 9 with proof 217-259 is the prerequisite of the already-adopted Main Theorem; its shadowing construction is already inside the 2158 H3 reason. Not recounted as an independent H2/H3 core.
Theorems 6 and 7 and Proposition 4 are external (Autissier, Zdunik, Milnor); quoting a strong tool is not by itself a new difficulty core.

core_recount_boundaries.item: no recount of definitions or context
core_recount_boundaries.literal: Definitions 1-3, the Chebyshev polynomial construction (88-92), the imaginary-quadratic/O_K notation (117), the characteristic exponent and Lyapunov exponent definitions (175-188) and the postcritical set (201-205) are setup, not separate problems.

Remark 8 (197-199) and Remark 10 (261-265) are commentary; the first delegates the argument to Z2014 and the second says 'one can show' while citing FG2022 and JX2022. Promoting either would require supplying author-omitted mathematics.

core_recount_boundaries.item: no candidate from the comparison results
core_recount_boundaries.literal: Theorem 5 (Ji-Xie) and the prose on H2021, H2022 and Eremenko-van Strien (lines 134-145) are prior literature, not results of this work.

core_recount_boundaries.item: no difficulty inflation from external-tool overlap
core_recount_boundaries.literal: The H3 of 2158 rests on the descent plus shadowing plus Galois-orbit averaging plus rigidity chain; the presence of Autissier and Zdunik citations alone is not the reason, and no other environment in this short paper adds a second independent core.

author_unexpanded_or_open_ranges.note: interval plus finite set characteristic exponent closure; compared external stronger result retained, no standalone new unit

objects_that_must_not_be_silently_change: 'number field' must not be narrowed to 'imaginary quadratic field' or to Q (that is the content of the strengthening over Theorem 5)
the conclusion must not be narrowed to 'flexible Lattès map' (unlike Milnor's integer case where Proposition 4 makes integrality equivalent to flexibility)
the multiplier hypothesis is on all cycles of all periods, not only on fixed points
the map class is all degree >= 2 rational maps, not polynomials or unicritical maps
chi_f uses log of the absolute value of the multiplier divided by the exact period, not the multiplier itself

external_dependency_notes.role: moduli space algebraic over Q, multiplier-isospectral locus Zariski closed over K (Th. 2.1, Th. 4.5)
finiteness of classes with the same multipliers per period, plus the flexible Lattès curve (Cor. 2.3)
characterization via characteristic exponents exceeding L_f (Prop. 4), used in the strengthened infinite form
Milnor's integer-multiplier problem and the quoted Proposition 4; also cited for finite quotients of affine maps (Lem. 3.8)
Ji-Xie Theorem 1.13 and the comparison in Remark 10 (S2, Cor. 1.16)
background and analogous equidistribution references only
prior/related work mentioned in the introduction and Remark 10; not results of this work

producer_source_notation_points.note: The middle display uses r (the number of Galois translates chosen) while the outer normalization is |S_n|; the identification with (1/p_n) log|lambda_n| is not expanded. Recorded as printed; not modified, and no independent verdict on its validity is issued.

producer_source_notation_points.literal_phenomenon: 'there is a sequence (w_n)_{n \geq N} such that w_n is periodic for f with period n ... for all n \geq N'
producer_source_notation_points.note: Indexing starts at N inside a remark reporting Ji-Xie's result; printed as is.

producer_source_notation_points.literal_phenomenon: 'we have shown that chi_f(z_0) <= L_f for all but finitely many periodic points z_0'
producer_source_notation_points.note: The body of the proof established the inequality for repelling z_0 outside P_f; the extension to all but finitely many is stated in one sentence. Recorded as a quantifier/range point for the owner; the text is not altered.
Products are taken in the spherical norm; the transition between the two indexings uses f^{\circ j}(w_n) = g^{\circ (n-j)}(w_n) from line 220. Printed as is.

producer_source_notation_points.literal_phenomenon: for n >= N the map h \circ g^{\circ (n-l)} : V \to W induces a contraction of \overline{W}; exact period n is then proved for n >= max{N, 2l}
producer_source_notation_points.note: Two different lower bounds N and max{N,2l} appear for different assertions; retained as printed.

normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.evidence: The disjoint union at 284-286 explicitly has r cycles each of exact period p_n; the r/|S_n| normalization uses those declared objects. This is not evidence of missing author mathematics.
normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.retain_as: optional reading note, excluded from unresolved-source or author-contact list

normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.evidence: The quoted sequence is indexed n>=N and has period n for n>=N. The two uses agree literally.

The final sentence compresses the passage from repelling periodic points outside the postcritical set to the cofinite periodic-point conclusion. No source-marked omission is asserted; turning this into a gap would re-audit the old H3 proof, outside this review.
normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.retain_as: preserve the exact original sentence and cited Theorem 7 dependence, exclude from author-omission inventory; do not insert the producer's explanatory finite-exception text as if it were literal source

normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.evidence: The spherical derivative product is reindexed using the identity already displayed at 220; its ranges are different descriptions of the same source orbit segment.
n>=N constructs the contraction fixed point; n>=max{N,2l} is subsequently used to establish its exact period. The source distinguishes these roles.

producer_author_unexpanded_or_open_range.literal: 'her proof can be easily modified to obtain the statement above' and 'the remainder of [Proof of Prop. 4]{Z2014} shows that ...' - the modified argument is described, not written out

'one can show that ... the closure of the set of characteristic exponents of f at its cycles is the union of an interval and a finite set (compare [Proof of Lem. 2.1]{FG2022})' - asserted without proof in this work; the sharper non-singleton statement is attributed to JX2022 Cor. 1.16
